policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads 'on one of the days' with no demonstrative; the added ἐκείνων would give 'those days'.
ASV 'the chief priests' renders ἀρχιερεῖς; ἱερεῖς would be simply 'the priests'.
ASV 'they spake, saying unto him' renders a participle λέγοντες alongside the main verb, which excludes r02's omission; the relative order of λέγοντες and πρὸς αὐτόν leaves no trace in English.
ASV 'a question' carries no numeral; the added ἕνα, an attributive numeral, would be rendered 'one question'.
ὁ λαὸς ἅπας and πᾶς ὁ λαός are both 'all the people'; the difference is Greek word order only.
ASV 'A man planted a vineyard' renders Ἄνθρωπος and Ἄνθρωπός τις alike, since τις here is the indefinite marker English carries with 'a'.
ASV 'at the season' renders the bare dative and ἐν with the dative identically.
ASV 'that they should give' fits the future δώσουσιν and the aorist subjunctive δῶσιν in a ἵνα clause alike.
ASV 'beat him, and sent him away empty' reports both actions; which participle-verb order the Greek used leaves no trace in English.
Word order of ἕτερον and πέμψαι only; ASV 'he sent yet another servant' renders either.
Word order of τρίτον and πέμψαι only; ASV 'he sent yet a third' renders either.
ASV 'it may be they will reverence him' has nothing for the added ἰδόντες ('when they see him').
ASV 'reasoned one with another' renders the reciprocal ἀλλήλους; the reflexive ἑαυτούς would be 'among themselves'.
ASV 'let us kill him' has nothing for δεῦτε ('come').
ASV names 'the scribes and the chief priests' in that order, matching γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς.
ASV 'they feared the people' renders τὸν λαόν, which the RP reading omits.
All three readings contain the same words; ASV 'he spake this parable against them' follows English order and cannot show where εἶπεν stood.
ASV shifts construction to 'so as to deliver him up' after the purpose clause 'that they might take hold', rendering result ὥστε rather than a second purpose εἰς τό.
ASV 'lawful for us to give' renders either case of the pronoun with δοῦναι.
ASV has nothing for the added Τί με πειράζετε ('Why tempt ye me?').
ASV 'Show me' renders the simplex and the ἐπι- compound imperative alike.
ASV 'And they said, Caesar's' has no 'answered'; ἀποκριθέντες would give 'they answered and said'.
'unto them' renders πρὸς αὐτούς and αὐτοῖς alike, and ASV's 'Then render' is the natural English for τοίνυν in either position.
ASV reads 'take hold of the saying', not 'his saying', matching τοῦ ῥήματος.
ASV 'they that say that there is no resurrection' renders the simple λέγοντες; ἀντιλέγοντες would give 'who deny' or 'who speak against'.
ASV keeps 'die' for the earlier ἀποθάνῃ and reads 'and he be childless' for the copula ᾖ; the RP reading repeats 'die childless'.
ASV verse 30 is only 'and the second:'; the RP expansion ('took the wife, and he died childless') is wholly absent.
ASV has a single 'likewise', attached to the seven; the added ὡσαύτως after αὐτήν would give a second one with the third brother.
ASV 'Afterward the woman also died' has nothing for πάντων ('last of all').
Both readings hold the same words; ASV fronts 'In the resurrection therefore' as English idiom and does not show whether ἡ γυνή preceded ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει.
ASV 'And Jesus said unto them' has nothing for ἀποκριθεὶς ('answering').
γαμίσκονται and ἐκγαμίσκονται are both 'are given in marriage'.
γαμίζονται and ἐκγαμίζονται are both 'are given in marriage'.
ASV 'for neither can they die any more' renders οὐδέ and οὔτε alike.
ASV 'sons of God' requires no English article, so the presence or absence of τοῦ before θεοῦ leaves no trace.
English supplies 'the' before 'God of Isaac' regardless of whether the Greek repeats the article.
English supplies 'the' before 'God of Jacob' regardless of whether the Greek repeats the article.
ASV opens 'For they durst not', rendering γάρ; δέ would give 'And'.
ASV “the Christ is David’s son” follows English order and does not show the order of εἶναι, Δαυίδ and υἱόν.
ASV 'For David himself saith' renders αὐτὸς γάρ; καὶ αὐτός would give 'And David himself'.
English requires 'The Lord' whether or not the Greek prefixes the article to κύριος.
ASV 'calleth him Lord' fixes the English order and does not show whether αὐτόν preceded κύριον.
ASV 'his son' renders either order of αὐτοῦ and υἱός.
ASV reads 'his disciples' with 'his' unitalicized, rendering the possessive αὐτοῦ.
